entrance.waived_by: a Texas State Parks Pass, which also covers the holder's guests

note_add: Each park sets its own daily entrance fee per person 13 and older, $0-8 (children 12 and under free); the amounts are on the entries. The $70 Texas State Parks Pass covers the holder and their guests for a year. Most park campsite pages allow two vehicles a site (an RV counts as one) and charge extra vehicles in an overflow lot at a per-park rate ($3-10 a night), and allow up to 8 people a site. No page read names a reservation fee; a camping change or cancellation costs a $10 penalty (5+ days out) or $10 a night up to $50 (under 5 days), entrance fees excluded.

unsettled.entrance.amount: Set park by park, $0-8 per person 13+ a day (already on each entry; tx_build.py read every park's page 2026-10-12). Whether the departure day is charged too is not stated on any page read.
unsettled.reservation_fee: No TPWD page read names one (reservation, FAQ and cancellation pages); a 2010 TPWD newsletter says the online booking fee was eliminated, but no current page says there is none, so no zero.
unsettled.tax: No TPWD statement. A 1986 Comptroller letter ruling (via a third-party site) treated campsite fees as exempt from hotel tax; not a current primary source.
unsettled.nonresident: No non-resident camping rate appears on any park page, but no page says there is none.
unsettled.extra_vehicle: Per park: most pages allow two vehicles and charge extras $3-10 a night in overflow; no statewide rule.
unsettled.extra_person: Most park pages say 'People per Site: 8', but it is posted per site type, not as a statewide rule, and no page says extra people are free.

summary: TX: entrance is per person 13+ per day at a per-park amount ($0-8, on the entries); $70 annual pass covers holder and guests. Reservation fee, tax, extra vehicle/person not settled.

note_add: A camping reservation includes one vehicle's parking pass, so the camper pays no parking fee; each further vehicle buys its own pass for the length of the stay. Only the parks that charge for parking (about two dozen of them) sell passes: TravelOK's parking-pass guide lists a one-day pass at $10 ($8 discounted rate), with three-day, week and annual options (read from a search summary, the page no longer loads).

unsettled.nonresident: None seen; no page says there is none.
unsettled.extra_person: No statewide occupancy or per-person rule found (OAC 725:30 has only McGee Creek's 12-person cap).

summary: OK: the reservation includes one vehicle's parking pass (camper entrance 0); extra vehicles buy their own pass at the parks that charge. Reservation fee and tax not settled.

note_add: Every vehicle in the park needs its own vehicle permit, a towed car included. The camping permit is per camping unit, so a second tent or camper on a site pays a second camping fee.

tax.name: Nebraska state and local sales tax plus lodging tax

note_add: A daily park entry permit runs until noon the day after activation, so one covers one night. Every vehicle needs its own permit; a site holds one camping unit with one tent (or two tents) and one tow or towed vehicle, and extra vehicles park in designated lots. Up to 8 people a site unless the superintendent allows more; additional tents or occupants may be charged an additional camping fee. Tax is added on top of the posted rates and on the reservation fee: state and local sales tax on RV sites plus lodging tax (tent-only sites pay lodging tax only), so the rate varies by location. The reservation fee is per unit reserved, non-refundable. Lake McConaughy and Lake Ogallala charge $5 more Thursday-Saturday in season (on those entries).

summary: NE: entry permit $7/$14 confirmed in 163 NAC 5 (good to noon next day); 8 people a site; tax added on top (sales + lodging); $8.50 reservation fee per unit confirmed.

note_add: ARSD confirms the figures (rules amended Nov 11, 2024). A site holds one camper unit: a family, or a party of six or fewer; the manager may let two units (12 people at most) share a site at twice the camping fee. Camping fees are per camper unit, with no per-person charge outside Custer's French Creek natural area and group camps. Each vehicle needs its own entrance licence.

summary: SD: existing values confirmed in ARSD - entrance $10/$15 per vehicle (a camper's daily licence runs to 4 p.m. next day), no online reservation fee for residents (phone $6), non-residents $10 per reservation.

note_add: Every vehicle needs a daily or annual vehicle entrance permit, campers included: $7 a day, $35 a year, $61.25 for a family annual permit (two household vehicles), one price for everyone; North Dakota residents 65+ pay $28 a year. Additional vehicles at a campsite pay the daily fee for each day in the park. A site takes one camping unit with up to six people, or the immediate family. Saturday nights cost $5 more on standard, modern and premium sites (on the entries).
